title: How to Spot a Fake Bill of Lading
summary: How trade finance and compliance teams spot a fake bill of lading, confirm it with the carrier, and catch cargo financed more than once.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** A fake bill of lading is a transport document forged, altered, or issued with false content to support payment, financing, or the movement of value. The[ICC International Maritime Bureau](https://icc-ccs.org/imb-nvocc-register-a-business-solution-to-a-business-problem/) says around 95 percent of the false bills it identifies are issued by non-vessel operating common carriers, or NVOCCs. No review of the file can prove that cargo exists, so a bill needs confirmation from the carrier and from sources outside the document set.


## What a Fake Bill of Lading Actually Is


A bill of lading is the document a carrier or its agent issues to acknowledge receipt of cargo for shipment. The[FATF and Egmont Group report on trade-based money laundering](https://www.fatf-gafi.org/content/dam/fatf-gafi/reports/Trade-Based-Money-Laundering-Trends-and-Developments.pdf) gives it three functions: a receipt for the goods, evidence of the contract of carriage, and a document of title.


Fake bills come in three classes. Edited-after-creation starts from a genuine bill and changes the consignee, the dates, the quantity, or the vessel. Generated-from-scratch has no carrier record behind it. The third class is the hardest: a genuine issuer signs a bill whose content is false. The IMB describes suspect bills as those carrying the wrong ship, dates, cargo description, container numbers, or parties.


The Bureau also says the vast majority of NVOCCs issue bills correctly, so an NVOCC name is a reason to confirm the issuer and proves nothing alone.


## Negotiable, Sea Waybill, or Electronic


The type of document determines what a forgery can steal. UNCTAD describes the negotiable bill as a document of title that gives its lawful holder the exclusive right to demand delivery in exchange for the original. A sea waybill needs no presentation at delivery, which UNCTAD says makes it unsuitable where a bank needs independent documentary security.


Document Title function How cargo is released What a financing bank should ask


Negotiable bill, to order Document of title, transferable by endorsement Against an original Does the bank hold the full set of originals?


Straight bill Names one consignee, with limited transfer Varies by law and by the bill's terms Which law governs, and must it be surrendered?


Sea waybill Receipt and contract evidence, no title To the named consignee, with no document presented What security stands in for it?


Electronic bill Equivalent to paper where law and system allow To the party in control of the record Who controls the record on the platform today?


Electronic bills change the question from who holds the paper to who controls the record. The[UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records](https://uncitral.un.org/en/texts/ecommerce/modellaw/electronic_transferable_records) treats exclusive control, established by a reliable method, as the equivalent of possession. UNCITRAL's status page lists legislation based on or influenced by the Model Law in 13 States, including the UK's Electronic Trade Documents Act. A PDF of an electronic bill is only a picture of the record, so the check has to happen on the platform. In the FIT Alliance's 2026 survey, 22.2% of bank respondents reported at least partial use.


## What a Forged Bill Is Used For


Common uses of a false bill are drawing under a documentary credit, raising invoice or receivables finance, obtaining release of cargo from an agent, and supporting a payment that has no real trade behind it.


FATF and Egmont name phantom shipments, where no goods move at all, and the reuse of documents to justify multiple payments for one shipment, sometimes across several institutions.[Trade-based money laundering](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/what-is-trade-based-money-laundering) covers those techniques in full. Sanctions evasion is the other driver. OFAC's 2020 maritime advisory lists falsified shipping documents among the practices used to disguise origin.


## Reading the Bill Against the Rest of the Set


Start with whether the set agrees with itself. Compare the bill with the commercial invoice, the packing list, and the credit: parties, ports, vessel, shipment date, goods description, quantity, weight, marks, and container numbers. UCP 600 article 14(d) says data need not be identical but must not conflict, so a bill saying "hats" sits fine beside an invoice for green hats, and one saying red hats does not.


Checking for compliance and checking for fraud are separate jobs. Under UCP 600, banks deal in documents and disclaim responsibility for genuineness and for the existence of the goods. A presentation can comply on its face and describe nothing real. The FFIEC BSA/AML manual expects banks, to the extent feasible, to review documents for anomalies as well as compliance. The commercial side has its own tests, covered in[how to spot a fake invoice](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-invoice) .


Goods out of line with the customer's business and routes with no obvious logic justify a closer look. Practitioners quoted by Global Trade Review note that duplicate or switched bills can have commercial reasons, such as a trader concealing its supplier, so a second bill needs an explanation before it becomes a finding.


## Checks That Reach Outside the File


### The carrier, reached independently


Confirm the bill with the carrier through a contact the bank found itself, covering the bill number, vessel, voyage, loading date, parties, and containers. Do not rely on a link or QR code printed on the bill. In 2012 the IMB described fake carrier websites that confirmed loading for cargo that never moved, one of them closely copying a major liner company's site. For a house bill issued by an NVOCC, also ask the ocean carrier about the shipment behind it.


### Container numbers and the check digit


Under ISO 6346, a container number has a three-letter owner code, an equipment letter, six serial digits, and a check digit. The Bureau International des Containers runs a public calculator and the owner code register. A failed check digit means a mistyped or invented number. A passing check digit proves only that the number is well formed. Leasing also means the owner code need not match the carrier.


### The vessel and the IMB


Vessel checks test whether the voyage could have happened. A vessel's IMO number is meant to stay with it through changes of name and owner. The ICC's 2026 vessel checking guide advises validating vessel movements through competent third parties when defined risk indicators are triggered, and treats a shipment that could not have occurred as an indicator of falsified documentation. AIS tracks position, and OFAC warns it can be disabled or spoofed. A ship in the right port on the right day still says nothing about what it loaded.


The IMB authenticates transport documents for members by making independent checks with named parties and others, and members can see whether an NVOCC has signed its Code of Conduct.


### Proving there was cargo


Even a genuine bill may not establish what is in the box. The ICC guide notes that containerized goods are described as the shipper states, without carrier verification, which is what "said to contain" means. Cargo evidence comes from outside the bill: an independent inspection at loading, terminal or customs records, and, as the FFIEC suggests, official import and export forms.


## The Same Cargo, Financed Twice


Multiple financing uses documents that may each look perfect, which is why one bank's review cannot catch it.[Global Trade Review's account of the Hin Leong collapse](https://www.gtreview.com/news/asia/analysis-hin-leongs-vicious-cycle-of-trade-finance-fraud/) cites court-appointed managers who found bills for three parallel trades bearing the same vessel name and aggregate cargo, differing only in date. Liabilities reached around US$3.5 billion. The vessels were typically chartered by a group company, so the supporting paper came from the borrower's own side. In 2023, Singapore's High Court dismissed a US$60.9 million claim against two banks after finding the underlying bills forged.


Practical controls follow from that case. Hold the full set of originals where the product allows it, because finance against copies leaves title elsewhere. Ask who else finances the customer and compare stated cargo with the vessel's plausible capacity. Treat a carrier related to the borrower as a weak confirmation.


## How Detection Actually Works


[File analysis](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/pdf-metadata-analysis-fraud-detection) runs six checks: production method, timestamp trail against the shipment and issue dates, issuer matching against that carrier's real documents, consistency across the set, model artifacts, and recycled patterns across unrelated presentations.


Edited bills tend to fail on file history, and generated ones on issuer and pattern. A scan adds noise, since its dates record only the scanning. The hard limit is that file forensics cannot prove cargo exists or that a ship loaded it. A clean file from a complicit issuer can describe a shipment that never happened, and only the carrier, the terminal, customs, or an inspector can speak to that.


## What to Do with a Suspect File


Hold payment or release under the bank's procedures and keep the document as presented. Write down the specific conflict. Confirm the bill with the carrier on an independently sourced contact, run the container and vessel checks, and escalate to the IMB or a specialist where the value or corridor warrants it. Screen vessels and parties for sanctions throughout, and consider SAR obligations once the facts support it. For a scored read of the file's history ahead of those checks,[check the document](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) . The outside confirmation still decides.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can you verify a bill of lading is genuine?


Contact the carrier or its agent through independently found details and confirm the bill number, vessel, loading date, parties, and containers. Then compare it with the invoice, packing list, and credit. IMB members can also ask the Bureau to authenticate it.


### Does a valid container check digit prove a container is real?


No. The ISO 6346 check digit only validates that the number was recorded and transmitted accurately. A well-formed number can still belong to a container that never carried this cargo, so confirmation has to come from the carrier.


### Can a PDF analysis prove the cargo exists?


No. Forensics can show that a file was altered, but a clean file can still describe a shipment that never happened. Carrier confirmation, terminal or customs records, and independent inspection are the evidence that goods moved.


### What is the difference between a bill of lading and a sea waybill?


A negotiable bill of lading is a document of title, and the holder claims the goods by presenting an original. A sea waybill is a receipt and evidence of the contract, and the carrier delivers to the named consignee with no document presented, so it gives a bank no documentary security.
